mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) of more than 2% signals weakening household demand, which pressures corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where RSAFS falls > 2% over 2 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals improving manufacturing activity and stronger corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where INDPRO rises > 0.5% over 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 1-month decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 1% AND HOUST falls > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where both RSAFS and HOUST fall > 1% in 1 month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% signals stronger labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where PAYEMS rises > 0.5% over 2 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% over 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) of more than 2% combined with a concurrent 1-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals a synchronized weakening in both demand and supply, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 2% over 2 months AND INDPRO falls > 0.5% over 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where RSAFS falls > 2% over 2 months AND INDPRO falls > 0.5% over 1 month (t-test p > 0.05).
